source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 211: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and treatment isolation: use the identical model checkpoint, tokenizer, serving/runtime versions, decoding limits, request trace and output-length distribution, scheduler, batching policy, hardware/topology, drivers, power, and thermal envelope in both arms. Change only weight precision; hold activation and KV-cache precision, calibration procedure, prompts, and unrelated optimization passes fixed. Version bit width, group size, scales/zero-points, outlier policy, calibration provenance, held-out split, kernels, and fallback routes. Use an authorized disposable environment and redact sensitive telemetry.

Falsifiable hypothesis for scenario variant 211: at every predeclared concurrency, weight-only quantization reduces fully loaded cost per successful output token by a predeclared target while held-out quality, safety, and correctness and the TTFT and TPOT latency gates remain satisfied. Reject the claim if any hard gate fails or the confidence interval does not support the target; do not treat an estimate or a fallback-heavy run as causal evidence.

Keep calibration and held-out evaluation sets disjoint. After equal warm-up and compilation, preregister sample size, scoring rubric, stopping rule, exclusions, and confidence-interval method; run repeated randomized interleaved paired baseline/treatment trials. Measure peak and steady memory in GiB, TTFT and TPOT in ms, throughput in tokens/s, queueing and concurrency, cost per successful token with its cost components, quality/safety/correctness scores, errors, timeouts, OOMs, retries, partial outputs, cleanup, kernel selection/support, and fallback rates. Report distributions, units, request mix, and intervals.

Log and control thermal throttling, cache state, scheduler contention, compilation, request mix, retry policy, unsupported kernels, and background load; stratify or invalidate compromised trials. Run only an authorized bounded canary with redacted logs, define quality/latency/error/OOM rollback thresholds, stop on safety or correctness regression, and restore the known-good configuration. Required evidence includes versioned configs, raw per-request metrics, calibration/held-out provenance, kernel/fallback logs, failure/cleanup records, and rollback audit records. Results are provisional and require domain-expert review.
